coverage_note: State employees under State Personnel and Pensions Article Title 3, with the common rights, unfair labor practices and board provisions of the Public Employee Relations Act, State Government Article Title 22, which also covers public school and community college employees under the Education Article. County and municipal employees bargain, where they do, under local codes and separate statutes not covered by this row. Text is the Department of Legislative Services statute file for the 2027 regular session, captured October 12, 2026; where it shows two contingent versions, the version marked in effect is cited.

who_may_bargain.value: Employees with bargaining rights under State Personnel and Pensions Title 3 (most Executive Branch units, the University System and other listed institutions) or under the Education Article provisions for public school and community college employees.
who_may_bargain.quote: “Public employee” means an individual who holds a position by appointment or employment in the service of a public employer with collective bargaining rights under Title 3 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article or Title 6, Subtitle 4 or 5 or Title 16, Subtitle 7 of the Education Article.

scope_of_bargaining.value: For State employees: all matters relating to wages, hours and other terms and conditions of employment, plus access to new employee programs. The State need not negotiate matters inconsistent with law; agreements on them take effect only if the General Assembly amends the law.
scope_of_bargaining.quote: Collective bargaining shall include all matters relating to: (1) wages, hours, and other terms and conditions of employment; and (2) the time and manner of access to a new employee program in accordance with § 22–207 of the State Government Article.

impasse_procedure.value: For State employees: if negotiations for the next fiscal year are not concluded before October 25, either party may request a neutral fact finder, who makes written recommendations before November 20 that go to the Governor and legislative leaders. BWI Airport firefighters have last-best-offer arbitration instead. Recommendations are not binding.
impasse_procedure.quote: (ii) If the parties do not conclude negotiations for the next fiscal year before October 25, either party may request that a fact finder be employed to resolve the issues.
impasse_procedure.pinpoint: Md. Code, State Pers. & Pens. 3-501 (paragraph (3)(ii), version in effect)

agency_fee_status.value: None. The Act provides only for membership dues deduction on the employee's assent, and Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees.
agency_fee_status.quote: (a) An employee organization is entitled to membership dues deduction, on presentation by the employee organization of: (1) dues deduction authorization cards; (2) electronic membership application; or (3) other method by which an employee has manifested assent for membership dues deduction.
